items.title: Colombia announces withdrawal from Hague Group, citing body’s actions over Israel
items.desc: The Hague ​Group of countries ​says it seeks to uphold international law and processes, including ​in the International Criminal ​Court over Israel’s actions.

items.title: Roads around Kirtipur cricket ground to be blacktopped within three months
items.desc: The Kathmandu Road Division has invited bids for upgrading 1.5km of access roads at an estimated cost of Rs69.8 million, ahead of international cricket tournaments.

items.title: Janakpur bowlers restrict Karnali to 132
items.desc: Captain Harmeet Singh takes three wickets as Karnali Yaks lose nine wickets in their 20 overs in the Nepal Premier League.

items.title: Kathmandu Valley to consume 5.18 million flower garlands this Tihar
items.desc: Domestic growers are expected to meet nearly 89 percent of demand as the festival’s flower trade, including plants and potted chrysanthemums, approaches Rs645 million.

items.title: Nepali lawmaker faces privacy backlash over videos of children filmed with smart glasses
items.desc: Ashika Tamang blurred a child’s face after criticism, but rights advocates say her videos raise wider questions about consent and the responsibilities of elected representatives.

items.title: Attackers kill 60 people in Ethiopia’s conflict-hit Oromiya region, Orthodox church says
items.desc: The ​Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said ​14 believers were killed in Merti Woreda on October 20 and 46 in Sherka Woreda on October 24.

items.title: Fastest turnout in 45 years as Israelis pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
items.desc: The Central Elections Committee reported that 16.7 percent of eligible voters had already cast their ballots within the first three hours, the fastest early turnout rate since 1981.

items.title: Handigaun Jatra: A jatra like no other
items.desc: Handigaun’s three-day festival features upside-down chariot spires, wax flowers and a legend about a woman who endured 12 years of labour.

items.title: Chitwan Rhinos defeat Biratnagar Kings by eight runs
items.desc: Kamal Singh Airee took four wickets as Biratnagar fell short of a 158-run target despite Andre Russell’s late 33 off 17 balls.

items.title: The NPL is on, but fans in Achham can’t get a signal
items.desc: As the tournament unfolds in Kathmandu, supporters in remote villages are travelling to nearby settlements and market centres to watch their teams.

items.title: Nepal gives 35 days to agency owners yet to respond to arrest warrants
items.desc: The Department of Foreign Employment warns of banking and travel restrictions for those who fail to report, as it investigates Malaysia’s selection of 25 Nepali recruitment agencies.

items.title: Biratnagar Kings need 158 to win
items.desc: Losing the toss and batting first, Chitwan Rhinos managed 157/3 in the first innings on the back of Dawid Malan’s 70 off 50.

items.title: How Pakistan’s NOC rules are affecting the Nepal Premier League
items.desc: A reported $25,000 clearance demand has disrupted team plans, leaving franchises uncertain about the availability of seven Pakistani players signed for the tournament.

items.title: Nepalis in Saudi Arabia urged to follow security alerts amid drone attacks
items.desc: The embassy in Riyadh calls for vigilance and warns against sharing unverified reports as missile and drone threats persist.

items.title: Nepal’s historic loss and damage allocation falls short of its needs
items.desc: The UN fund has provisionally set aside 21.6 million for Nepal after the Rasuwa disaster, marking a first while covering less than 0.5 percent of the country’s estimated $4.7 billion recovery and reconstruction needs.

items.title: Nepal plans first feasibility study for Himalayan tourism highway
items.desc: The proposed routes would connect Badimalika in the west and Pathibhara in the east, with a six-month study to assess costs, environmental impacts and possible road alignments.

items.title: Activist arrested over protest against Ani Choying Drolma’s appointment
items.desc: Police detained the head of a campaign opposing the appointment of the Buddhist nun as vice-chair of the Lumbini Development Trust after protesters burned a photograph of the tourism minister.

items.title: England forward Kane crowned Ballon d’Or winner, Putellas wins women’s award
items.desc: A 61-goal season for Bayern earns Kane his first Ballon d’Or, 25 years after Michael Owen became the last English winner, while Spain’s Alexia Putellas claims the women’s award for a third time.

items.title: Biratnagar take on Chitwan as Janakpur face Karnali in NPL double-header
items.desc: Andre Russell and Angelo Mathews add star power to Biratnagar, while former champions Janakpur look to bounce back after a disappointing second season.

items.title: Trump approval rises from record low to 32% ahead of midterm election, Reuters Ipsos poll finds
items.desc: Democrats hold an 11-point lead over Republicans in the congressional vote, while concerns over the cost of living weigh on Trump ahead of the November 3 midterms.

items.title: Restore hope for Bhotekoshi flood victims
items.desc: The Bhotekoshi flood victims deserve answers; they cannot remain in uncertainty any longer.

items.title: Devoid of options, flood survivors return to damaged homes
items.desc: The government has announced rent assistance, temporary shelters and new land for resettlement. Survivors and local officials say little of it has reached them.

items.title: She climbed Everest without supplemental oxygen. But the summit was never the point
items.desc: Melissa Arnot Reid, the first American woman to achieve the feat, launched her memoir in Kathmandu, reflecting on shame, self-worth and the people behind Himalayan expeditions.

items.title: After years of delay, Budhigandaki faces another change of plan
items.desc: Successive governments have changed the project’s development models. Latest plan to set up an authority has raised new questions over implementation.

items.title: Oli, Dahal move to extend alliance to next year’s local and provincial polls
items.desc: UML and Nepali Communist Party leaders are exploring grassroots-level electoral cooperation to prevent further erosion of left-wing support.

items.title: Xtreme is betting on Nepali sport. It’s helping both — for now
items.desc: A Nepali energy drink is now sponsoring national cricket team players, seven NPL franchises, and the country’s first franchise volleyball league. But nobody will say how much it is paying.
